mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly compares adipose tissue with areolar connective tissue?

options.A: Adipose tissue consists of tightly packed adipocytes that store fat, whereas areolar tissue has loosely arranged fibers and many cells, providing cushioning and flexibility.
options.B: Adipose tissue contains abundant collagen fibers for structural support, while areolar tissue primarily stores lipids.
options.C: Both adipose and areolar tissues have a liquid matrix, but adipose tissue is more vascular than areolar tissue.
options.D: Adipose tissue is found only under the skin, whereas areolar tissue is only present in the bone marrow.

mcqs.answer: Adipose tissue consists of tightly packed adipocytes that store fat, whereas areolar tissue has loosely arranged fibers and many cells, providing cushioning and flexibility.
mcqs.explanation: Adipose tissue is made up of large, tightly packed fat‑storing cells (adipocytes) with little extracellular matrix, giving it a role in energy storage and insulation. Areolar tissue, a loose connective tissue, has a sparse network of collagen and elastic fibers with many cells, allowing it to act as a cushion and provide flexibility. The other options misstate the composition or location of these tissues.

mcqs.question: Which statement best explains how the structure of dense regular connective tissue determines its function?

options.A: Dense regular connective tissue has a random arrangement of collagen fibers, allowing it to resist forces from all directions.
options.B: Loose connective tissue contains densely packed fibers that give it high tensile strength.
options.C: In dense regular connective tissue, collagen fibers are aligned parallel, providing high tensile strength in one direction, ideal for tendons.
options.D: Elastic connective tissue’s fibers are arranged in sheets, making it suitable for bone formation.

mcqs.answer: In dense regular connective tissue, collagen fibers are aligned parallel, providing high tensile strength in one direction, ideal for tendons.
mcqs.explanation: Dense regular connective tissue is characterized by tightly packed collagen fibers that run parallel to each other. This arrangement gives the tissue great tensile strength along the direction of the fibers, making it perfect for structures like tendons and ligaments that transmit force in a single direction. Options A, B, and D describe incorrect structures or functions for the tissue type.

mcqs.question: Blood is classified as a connective tissue because:

options.A: It contains a solid extracellular matrix that provides structural support.
options.B: It has a liquid extracellular matrix (plasma) that transports cells and nutrients.
options.C: It is composed mainly of tightly packed muscle fibers.

mcqs.answer: It has a liquid extracellular matrix (plasma) that transports cells and nutrients.
mcqs.explanation: All connective tissues have cells separated by an extracellular matrix. In blood, the matrix is the fluid plasma, which carries blood cells and dissolved substances. This fulfills the definition of a connective tissue. Options A, C, and D are inaccurate descriptions of blood.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly describes a characteristic of bone tissue?

options.A: Bone tissue has a soft, gelatinous matrix that allows flexibility.
options.B: Bone cells are not embedded in any matrix.
options.C: Bone tissue is avascular and receives nutrients by diffusion.
options.D: Bone contains a hard, mineralized matrix that provides support and protection.

mcqs.answer: Bone contains a hard, mineralized matrix that provides support and protection.
mcqs.explanation: Bone tissue is a dense connective tissue with a matrix hardened by calcium phosphate crystals, giving it rigidity and the ability to support the body and protect vital organs. It is actually well vascularized, contrary to option C, and its cells (osteocytes) reside in lacunae within the matrix, contrary to option B.

mcqs.question: Cartilage differs from bone in that:

options.A: Cartilage lacks blood vessels, so it receives nutrients by diffusion, whereas bone is vascular.
options.B: Cartilage contains a mineralized matrix like bone.
options.C: Cartilage cells are called osteocytes, while bone cells are chondrocytes.
options.D: Cartilage is more rigid than bone due to higher collagen content.

mcqs.answer: Cartilage lacks blood vessels, so it receives nutrients by diffusion, whereas bone is vascular.
mcqs.explanation: Cartilage is avascular; nutrients diffuse from surrounding tissues, which limits its thickness and repair capacity. Bone, on the other hand, has a rich blood supply that supports growth and remodeling. Options B, C, and D incorrectly describe the composition and cell types of cartilage and bone.

mcqs.question: A doctor needs a connective tissue that can hold organs in place while allowing them to move freely. Which tissue is most suitable?

options.A: Dense regular connective tissue, because it provides strong attachment between muscles and bones.
options.B: Adipose tissue, because it stores energy and insulates organs.
options.C: Areolar tissue, because its loosely arranged fibers allow organs to be held loosely yet move freely.
options.D: Cartilage, because it provides a hard protective covering.

mcqs.answer: Areolar tissue, because its loosely arranged fibers allow organs to be held loosely yet move freely.
mcqs.explanation: Areolar tissue is a loose connective tissue with a meshwork of collagen and elastic fibers, providing both support and flexibility, making it ideal for surrounding organs. Dense regular tissue is too rigid, adipose tissue mainly stores fat, and cartilage is hard and unsuitable for this purpose.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is an example of a function performed by adipose tissue?

options.A: Providing structural support to the skeleton.
options.B: Storing excess energy as fat in the subcutaneous layer.
options.C: Facilitating rapid transmission of nerve impulses.
options.D: Producing red blood cells in the marrow.

mcqs.answer: Storing excess energy as fat in the subcutaneous layer.
mcqs.explanation: Adipose tissue is specialized for energy storage; it accumulates triglycerides in adipocytes, especially beneath the skin (subcutaneous) and around organs. It also provides insulation and cushioning. The other options describe functions of bone, nervous tissue, and bone marrow respectively.

mcqs.question: A sprinter suffers a tear in the Achilles tendon during a race. Which property of the tendon’s connective tissue best explains its susceptibility to this injury?

options.A: Loose connective tissue’s random fiber arrangement gives high elasticity, preventing tendon injuries.
options.B: Elastic connective tissue’s abundant elastin fibers make tendons highly stretchable.
options.C: Cartilage’s dense matrix makes tendons resistant to tearing.
options.D: Dense regular connective tissue’s parallel collagen fibers give high tensile strength but limited elasticity, making tendons prone to strain injuries.

mcqs.answer: Dense regular connective tissue’s parallel collagen fibers give high tensile strength but limited elasticity, making tendons prone to strain injuries.
mcqs.explanation: Tendons are composed of dense regular connective tissue where collagen fibers run parallel, providing great tensile strength for force transmission. However, this arrangement offers limited stretch, so sudden excessive force can cause tears. Options A, B, and C incorrectly describe the tissue type of tendons.
